$comment: RAG chatbot — query-path dashboard (NFR-8, implementation.md 5.6). Grafana-format, PostgreSQL datasource. Every query is written against the real schema in app/db/models.py: QueryLog(created_at, ttft_ms, total_ms, abstained, citations_stripped, tokens_in, tokens_out, feedback) and Document(state, byte_size, indexed_at, chunk_count, created_at).
title: RAG — Query path

panels.$comment: p50/p95/p99 of client-visible TTFT. The 5 s NFR-1 line is the whole point of this panel: architecture.md 7.2 asks for the alert to fire at 4 s so there is lead time, but the target that must not be crossed is 5 s.
panels.title: TTFT percentiles (ms) — target p95 < 5000
panels.description: Time to first token, server-measured. Budget 5000 ms; the paired alert fires at 4000 ms.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '5m'), percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ttft_ms) AS p50, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ttft_ms) AS p95, percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ttft_ms) AS p99 FROM query_logs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND ttft_ms IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.$comment: Refusals are a health signal, not an error (PRD puts the healthy band at 10-30%). A drop to zero usually means retrieval is broken and everything is being refused, or the threshold is mis-set; a spike to 100% means the corpus stopped matching.
panels.title: Refusal rate (healthy band 10–30%)
panels.description: Share of answered queries that abstained on the evidence threshold. Tracked as a health signal, not an error.

targets.rawSql: SELECT avg(CASE WHEN abstained THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS refusal_rate FROM query_logs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: Total answer latency percentiles (ms)
panels.description: Full answer time, not first token. The gap between this and TTFT is generation time.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '5m'), percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total_ms) AS p50, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total_ms) AS p95 FROM query_logs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND total_ms IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.$comment: Refusals never call the model, so they return almost instantly. Their latency is a baseline for the non-generation path and should stay far below answered TTFT; if it rises, the cost is in retrieval or the request path, not the model.
panels.title: Refused-request latency percentiles (ms) — no generation
panels.description: Refusals short-circuit before the LLM, so this is the retrieval + request overhead only.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '5m'), percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ttft_ms) AS p50, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ttft_ms) AS p95 FROM query_logs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) AND abstained AND ttft_ms IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.$comment: The silent failure. architecture.md 7.2 calls this out specifically: a strip-rate spike means the model or prompt drifted, and it degrades answer quality without the user seeing an error — they just get fewer, worse citations. Ratio (stripped per query) is more stable than a raw sum, so both are shown.
panels.title: Citation strip rate (stripped markers per query)
panels.description: Citations the validator removed as invalid. Any sustained rise is model or prompt drift degrading answers silently.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '5m'), avg(citations_stripped) AS strip_mean, max(citations_stripped) AS strip_max FROM query_logs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.$comment: Feedback lives on QueryLog (FR-29). The up/(up+down) ratio over time shows quality drift that users noticed, which is the counterpart to strip rate drifting below the user's awareness.
panels.title: User feedback ratio (up / (up + down))
panels.description: Thumbs up share of cast votes. Sustained decline means answers are getting worse.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '15m'), avg(CASE WHEN feedback = 'up' THEN 1.0 WHEN feedback = 'down' THEN 0.0 END) FILTER (WHERE feedback IN ('up','down')) AS up_ratio FROM query_logs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Token throughput (in / out per minute)
panels.description: Proxy for provider cost and for the load the model is actually absorbing.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '1m'), sum(tokens_in) AS tokens_in, sum(tokens_out) AS tokens_out FROM query_logs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Query volume
panels.description: Total and answered (non-refused) queries per minute. Latency percentiles are only meaningful alongside volume — a p95 computed from six requests is noise.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(created_at, '1m'), count(*) AS total, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT abstained) AS answered FROM query_logs WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
